title: Edge Analytics — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-grade methods developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Analyzing data where it is born: real-time analytics on fog nodes instead of the distant cloud. Edge analytics runs analytical workloads — filtering, aggregation, anomaly detection, dashboards, descriptive statistics — on fog nodes near the data source rather than shipping raw streams to a central cloud. The payoff is lower latency, lower backhaul bandwidth, and continued operation when the wide-area link is down. Typical pipelines: ingest on the gateway, window the stream, compute rolling features, trigger local alerts, and forward compact summaries upstream. Signature method: Signature Rolling Evidence: every window carries a compact proof (count, checksum, threshold crossings) so upstream merges stay auditable without re-shipping raw data.

title: Edge Analytics — Safety, limits, and failure modes
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-grade methods developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Edge nodes cannot hold long history; windows are bounded by local memory. Complex models must be distilled before deployment. Clock skew across nodes complicates event-time windowing.
